newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Parliament, protesters prepare for Mandela speech.
newsitem.headline: Parliament, protesters prepare for Mandela speech.

text.p: Heavy security was in place around the South African parliament in Cape Town on Friday as President Nelson Mandela prepared to open the assembly for its first session under a new constitution.

Police sealed off streets around the parliament buildings and a military helicopter clattered overhead as MPs and their spouses, returning from the long Christmas break, greeted each other in the crowded corridors of the colonial-style building.

Demonstrators campaigning for better AIDS research and legalisation of marijuana said they would hold protests outside parliament and independent fishermen protesting against what they consider unfair fishing quotas planned to burn a boat in Cape Town harbour.
A radical Moslem group planned to demonstrate outside the Israeli embassy near parliament in solidarity with Palestinians.
Mandela was due to receive a national salute in front of parliament and army gunners on Table Mountain were scheduled to fire a 21-gun salute, followed by an air force fly-past.

Mandela was expected to begin delivering his speech at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) with media speculation focusing on what his government plans to do to accelerate economic reform, promote growth and curb rampant crime.
South Africa's financial markets were on Friday downgrading expectations of a major announcement on exchange controls from Mandela, dealers said.
"I think it will be a damp squib," said one bond trader of Mandela's speech. "I don't think they will announce anything big today, but our markets are still fundamentally positive."
Dealers said the rand and bonds had been feeding on each other recently, with a strong rand tempting overseas buyers back into South African debt and heavy bond buying boosting the currency.
